value.overview: The Gray-headed Chachalaca (Ortalis cinereiceps) is a medium-sized, long-tailed member of the chachalaca family, Cracidae. It has mostly gray-brown plumage, a dark gray head, chestnut flight feathers, and a red throat wattle. Usually living in small groups, it feeds mainly on fruit and leaves in dense vegetation. Its loud, rough calls often reveal its presence before the birds are seen. It is a resident species in Costa Rica.
value.classification: The Gray-headed Chachalaca belongs to the family Cracidae in the order Galliformes. It is one of the chachalacas, guans, and curassows, a group of mostly tropical forest birds.
value.identification: This chachalaca is about 48 centimeters long, with a small head, sturdy legs, broad rounded wings, and a long tail. Adults are generally grayish brown above and paler below, with a dark gray head, gray bill and legs, and dull red bare skin on the throat. The chestnut primary feathers are especially noticeable in flight. The tail is dark and has pale buff tips. Juveniles are browner overall, particularly on the head.
value.rangeHabitat: The species ranges from eastern Honduras and Nicaragua through Costa Rica and Panama to northwestern Colombia. In Costa Rica it is a resident of lowlands and foothills on both the Caribbean slope and the Pacific slope, extending southward from the western Central Valley and the Gulf of Nicoya region toward Panama. It commonly uses dense thickets, forest edges, river and stream margins, secondary woodland, brushy clearings, abandoned fields, and partially opened forest, generally from sea level to about 1,100 meters in Costa Rica.
value.migrationStatus: Resident and nonmigratory. Gray-headed Chachalacas occur in Costa Rica throughout the year rather than arriving as seasonal migrants, although local movements may follow food availability and water sources.
value.breeding: Breeding information from Costa Rica indicates nesting mainly from February through June. The nest is a broad, shallow platform made from twigs, vines, and other plant material, usually placed about 1 to 2.5 meters above the ground in a shrub, small tree, or tangle of vines. A clutch normally contains about three dull whitish eggs, sometimes two. The female generally performs the incubation, while adults may remain associated with small family groups.
value.dietFeeding: Fruit forms most of the diet, supplemented by leaves and smaller amounts of invertebrates. Gray-headed Chachalacas forage mainly in trees, shrubs, and tangled vegetation, but they sometimes descend to the ground. They may take berries, fleshy fruits, and other soft plant material, along with insects and similar prey. During dry periods, birds may visit rivers or streams to drink, especially in the morning and evening.
value.behavior: Gray-headed Chachalacas usually travel in loose groups of about six to twelve birds, sometimes forming larger gatherings. They are active and largely arboreal, moving through foliage and branches while feeding. Their calls are loud, harsh, and rhythmical, with groups often calling around dawn or dusk. They are generally less dependent on the interior of mature forest than many larger cracids and can use disturbed habitats when suitable dense cover remains.

conservation.populationTrend: No precise global population trend estimate is available, but the species remains fairly common to common across much of its range and is not currently considered globally threatened.
